subject: Transportation Systems
title: Search and Rescue at Sea
description: A fast breakdown of Search and Rescue at Sea for builders.

hook.text: When a ship sends a distress signal, the nearest vessel is legally obligated to help—no exceptions.

buildup.text: The Global Maritime Distress and Safety System uses satellites to relay alerts to rescue centers.

discovery.text: EPIRBs—emergency beacons—activate on contact with water and transmit the ship's exact position.

twist.text: In remote oceans, rescue can take days. Survival suits and life rafts must keep people alive until then.

climax.text: Coordinated search areas are calculated from drift models, ocean currents, and wind patterns.

punchline.text: At sea, the duty to rescue is absolute.

quiz.question: What does an EPIRB do when activated?
options: Pumps water out of the hull
Transmits the ship's position via satellite
